title: The grid under strain
takeaway: Northern Illinois data centers crowd onto ComEd's 345 kV ring around Chicago, 76 to 223 km from the reactors that feed it, and one planned Yorkville campus would draw about as much power as the Dresden nuclear plant generates.
story: Federal records list 201 data centers in Illinois, grouped here into 42 sites. 38 of them are in ComEd's territory and 30 sit within 50 km of the Loop. Seven in ten are within 5 km of a 345-kilovolt line, the backbone that carries power in from reactors 76 to 223 km away.

The next wave is bigger. One planned campus in Yorkville lists 1,803 MW of demand, about the output of the Dresden plant. ComEd expects to spend more than $3 billion connecting data centers, and the Sun-Times counts 100 or more operating, under construction or proposed in northern Illinois.

peg.author: Brett Chase
peg.headline: Illinois' electric grid is under a lot of stress. What does that mean for consumers?

data_as_of: Data centers Sept. 2025; transmission lines 2021; nuclear capacity Aug. 2021
projection: Distances were measured in Illinois State Plane East (EPSG:3435), NAD83. The print plate uses Albers equal-area conic; this web layer is drawn in Web Mercator.
alt: A map of northern Illinois from the Mississippi River to Lake Michigan. A grey wash covers ComEd's service area. Dark lines show the 345-kilovolt transmission network, which forms a ring around Chicago with spokes out to six nuclear plants. Orange circles mark 42 data center sites, most clustered along the lines near O'Hare and the Loop. One large pale circle west of Aurora marks a planned Yorkville campus listing 1,803 megawatts.

method: Data centers are clipped to Illinois. Listings within 1.5 km of each other are grouped into one site (single linkage). A site is drawn as mostly operating or mostly planned by the majority of its listings. Circle area is proportional to the number of listings.
Distances are straight-line: site to the nearest 345 kV+ line, site to the nearest nuclear plant, and each plant to the Loop (41.878°N, 87.630°W).
The build stops if a figure in the story no longer matches the data (see checks in layer.json).
caveats: The federal inventory undercounts the new wave. It shows 42 Illinois sites; the Sun-Times counts 100 or more. Campuses announced in 2026, such as PowerHouse Joliet, T5 Grayslake, Tract Morris and Compass Hoffman Estates, are missing.
Planned power totals are floors, because 37 planned listings give no figure. The federal power_demand field has no stated unit; its match to the Yorkville campus supports reading it as megawatts.
Transmission data dates from 2021 and is generalized to about 400 m. Lines built since then are missing.
Nuclear capacity is nameplate as of 2021. Recent uprates are not reflected. The operator then listed as Exelon is now Constellation.
Being near a 345 kV line does not mean a site connects to it. The map shows proximity only.
The Yorkville campuses face litigation (spring 2026), so the site is planned, not certain.
